newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds Metals reorganizes into six units from 20.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds Metals reorganizes into six units from 20.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co., which lost money late last year while rivals were reporting profits, said Thursday it was reorganizing into six units to focus on the world's most profitable aluminum markets.

"Reynolds business focus is now on those markets that have the greatest potential for market and geographic growth into the next century," Chairman Jeremiah J. Sheehan said in a statement announcing the restructuring.
He said Reynolds, which had been organised into 20 operating units, would be restructured into six worldwide, market-focused businesses, effective April 1.

The company, which reported a loss eqal to 13 cents a share for the 1996 fourth quarter, named the executives who will head the new divisions but did not disclose other details about the reorganization.
It said it would announce further details within the next three months.
The company said Randolph N. Reynolds, vice chairman and executive officer, will have responsibility for four of the new global business units.

Reporting to him will be Donald T. Cowles, who will head a construction and distribution unit; Eugene M. Desvernine, who will be in charge of transportation; Paul Ratki, in charge of metals and carbon products; and Larry Hawkins, chief of bauxite and alumina operations.
It added that Thomas P. Christino will have responsibility for Reynolds global packaging and consumer products business and William E. Leahey Jr. will head the global can business.
Reynolds also said a spin-off of its packaging business was still under review.
"If and when we decide to proceed with that option, our new organisation structure will better position that business for becoming an independent company," Sheehan said.
Reynolds stock added $1 to $64.25 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
